clue.text: Last traces of Black Country block walls in abandoned station

indicators.note: the final marks something leaves are its closing letters, so take the end of each word
to wall something is to surround it on every side, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: the closing letter of each of the two words
a slab is a flat block of stone or concrete

explanation.surface: A derelict railway station in the industrial West Midlands, with the last scraps of grime on its walls.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Country is an industrial area of the English West Midlands. 'Station' here is a space station, not a railway one: Skylab was abandoned and fell back to Earth in 1979.
explanation.definitionFit: Skylab was the first American space station, left unmanned after 1974 until its orbit decayed.

clue.text: Blow in the manner of marsupial

blocks.note: KO, a knockout, is a decisive blow in boxing
from French 'à la', in the style of

explanation.surface: Describing a punch thrown in the style of a boxing kangaroo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'À la' is borrowed French for 'in the manner of', as in 'à la carte'; the accent is ignored in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: This Australian tree-dwelling animal carries its young in a pouch, making it a pouched mammal.

clue.text: You and I climbing in holidays — one will be standing in mountain air

definitions.text: one will be standing in mountain air

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
being placed inside means one piece sits within another

blocks.note: leave is time off work, as in annual leave
the pronoun for you and me together

explanation.surface: Two people on a hiking holiday, climbing where the air is thin and someone has to stand still.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole cryptic phrase: 'standing' is the physicist's sense, a wave that stays in one place while air flows through it.
explanation.definitionFit: Air flowing over a ridge sets up stationary oscillations on its sheltered downwind side, a standing wave meteorologists know glider pilots exploit.

clue.text: Resists fine shelled food and drink

indicators.note: removing the shell strips the outer layer, leaving only the inside letters

blocks.note: to buck a trend is to resist it
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
pizza with its outer letters removed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Food' is a definition by example here: the solver must think of pizza before peeling it. 'Shelled food' looks like prawns or nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Buck's Fizz is a British cocktail of champagne mixed with orange juice, served at brunch and weddings.

clue.text: So few, say, travelling ancient road

indicators.note: things on the move get jostled out of their places, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Remarking on how few people travel along an old road these days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' but is simply part of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fosse Way is a Roman road in England running from Exeter to Lincoln, built nearly two thousand years ago.

clue.text: Riding site made Balfour go off keeping a couple of horses

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so extra letters are held inside the rest
food that has gone off is spoiled and broken down, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse; two of them

explanation.surface: A politician named Balfour being sent off at a horse-riding venue with a pair of mounts in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riding' is not horse riding: Yorkshire was historically split into Ridings, and this headland is in the East Riding. Arthur Balfour was a British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: This chalk promontory on the Yorkshire coast is a location within the East Riding, one of that county's historic divisions.

clue.text: Lecher brooded over attention in speech

indicators.note: spoken rather than written, so the words matter by their sound

blocks.note: a hen broods by sitting on eggs, and to lend an ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A lecherous man dwelling sulkily on whether anyone listens to his talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' places one word above the other in a down entry. 'Sat ear' said quickly approximates how many pronounce the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth satyrs were goat-legged woodland spirits famous for lust, so the word names any lustful man.

clue.text: One stopping outside plot leaves shed light on

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap from within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Latin ex, out of, as in ex-works
a plot is a scheme or plan
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone stopping outside a garden plot where the leaves have been shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot leaves shed' reads like gardening, but 'shed light on' is the definition and 'leaves' simply means 'results in'.
explanation.definitionFit: To illuminate a matter is to make it clear, which is what clarifying or making something understood amounts to.

clue.text: Obsessed about bubbly coed getting tense narrative

indicators.note: something bubbly is fizzing and agitated, so the letters are churned up
to be about something is to be around it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: anal, short for anal-retentive, means obsessively fussy
taken letter for letter
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone fixated on a lively female student who is growing nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: A coed is American slang for a female student at a mixed college; 'bubbly' and 'tense' both look like descriptions of her.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotal is the adjective for stories told from personal experience, so it describes something in story form.

clue.text: Terribly clean lines through Spanish city

indicators.note: something done terribly is done badly, leaving the letters in disorder
to line something is to cover its inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: via means by way of, through
taken letter for letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' looks like a noun, railway or painted lines, but it is a verb: the jumbled letters line the inside of the other word.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is the third-largest Spanish urban centre, on the Mediterranean coast, home of paella.

clue.text: Hint — start to price former editor’s liquid asset?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: a tip is a hint or piece of advice
the opening letter
ex means former, as in ex-wife

explanation.surface: A tip about the price of a retired editor's cash holdings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquid asset' normally means cash; here it is literal, a fluid that helps an editor, with the question mark flagging the wordplay. Tipp-Ex is a brand of white correction fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Correction fluid paints over typing mistakes, so for anyone fixing text on paper it is a very useful fluid.

clue.text: Large island, a result of volcanic activity, not the first seen by Japan

indicators.note: excluding the first means the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: J is the international vehicle code for Japan
lava, molten rock from a volcano, without its first letter

explanation.surface: Describing a big volcanic island and noting the Japanese view of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The volcanic setting fits the answer itself, which is studded with active volcanoes, so the surface tempts solvers to look for the island in the description.
explanation.definitionFit: Java is the Indonesian landmass holding Jakarta, one of the most populous islands in the world.

clue.text: Dog, overwhelmed by duties, bolted by river when recalled

indicators.note: being overwhelmed is being engulfed, so these letters are swallowed inside another word
recalling brings something back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: duties are obligations, things owed
bolted means ran off suddenly
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A dog, swamped by its chores, runs off along the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: The running and the river are inserted together into the obligations, then the whole thing is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The St Bernard is a large Alpine breed famed for mountain rescue, a giant working canine.

clue.text: Mercury and Venus conclude with tweaked notes, ending in unusual pair

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter
a tweaked thing has been adjusted, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: to infer is to conclude from evidence
taken letter for letter
the final letter
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A singer and a goddess, or a rock star and a tennis star, wrapping up a song with an odd duet.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercury and Venus suggest Freddie Mercury or a goddess, but they are the two planets nearer the Sun than Earth. 'Unusual' looks like an anagram signal but only supplies its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers call the planets orbiting inside Earth's path 'inferior', and only two qualify.

clue.text: Countryman’s wearing no pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are rubbishy and must be reworked

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A rustic fellow going about without trousers, or underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like a garment, but in British slang it means rubbish, and the 's after Countryman is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norwegian is a man belonging to a particular nation, here read as a man of a country rather than a rustic.

clue.text: Old cheese crackers dryish, oddly mellow

indicators.note: oddly means at the odd-numbered positions, the first, third and fifth letters
crackers means crazy, so the letters go wild

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A tasting note: aged cheese on crackers, rather dry but strangely mellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crackers' and 'cheese' pair naturally on a plate, hiding the anagram signal; 'Old' is part of the definition because the brand no longer exists.
explanation.definitionFit: Lymeswold was a mild English soft blue brand launched in 1982 and discontinued a decade later.

clue.text: One normally contributing to army manoeuvres?

definitions.text: One normally contributing to army manoeuvres?

blocks.note: surface reading: a soldier doing his bit in military exercises
setter's reading: 'army' as arm-y, movements of the arms, which a shoulder and back muscle helps make

explanation.walkthrough: 'Army' is turned into an adjective, to do with arms, and 'normally' points to the body working as it should rather than a soldier on duty.
explanation.definitionFit: This large back muscle moves the shoulder blades, so it plays a part in raising and rotating the upper limbs.

explanation.walkthrough: Norm looks like a name, and 'scrubbing' like cleaning, which suits the floor in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Parquet is wooden blocks laid in a geometric pattern as interior flooring.

clue.text: Core of virtuoso journalists stay for a day

explanation.definitionFit: A sojourn is a temporary residence, and the word comes from Latin for a day, so a short stopover fits.

the final letter

explanation.definitionFit: Abele is an old name for the white poplar, a species of broadleaf timber.
